summary: Extends the IMAP LIST command so a client can ask for STATUS information, such as message counts, in the same request. Without it, clients must list all mailboxes and then ask for status of each one separately. It is a proposed standard.

eli5.summary: Instead of asking for a list of boxes and then asking about each one, you ask for the list and counts in one go.

questions: get mailbox message counts with list
imap unseen count for all mailboxes
how to get message counts with imap list
what does the imap status return option do
subtitle: Lets an IMAP client list mailboxes and fetch their message counts in one command instead of one STATUS call per mailbox.

tldr.problem: Mail clients that show total and unseen counts must LIST all mailboxes and then send a STATUS command for each one, which wastes bandwidth and round trips.
tldr.mechanism: A new STATUS return option on the extended LIST command makes the server send an untagged STATUS response after each matching selectable mailbox's LIST response.
tldr.outcome: A client can get names and counts in a single request. Servers advertise the LIST-STATUS capability, and must take care not to starve other connections.

today: RFC 5819 is a Proposed Standard published in March 2010, and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why a LIST With STATUS
sections.content:
Many IMAP clients show the total number of messages and the number of unseen messages for each mailbox. To get them, they issue LIST or LSUB, then a STATUS command for every mailbox found.

RFC 3501 explicitly disallows mailbox patterns in STATUS, to discourage frequent use of an operation that can be expensive for a server. That prohibition backfired: clients now issue a STATUS for every mailbox that LIST returns, which wastes bandwidth and, for clients without IMAP pipelining, costs extra round trips.
sections.eli5: It is like asking a librarian for a list of shelves, then walking back to ask how many books are on each shelf, one shelf at a time. This RFC lets you ask both at once.

sections.title: The STATUS Return Option
sections.content:
The RFC extends the LIST command from RFC 5258 with a new return option, STATUS, that takes STATUS data items as parameters. For each selectable mailbox matching the pattern and selection options, the server MUST return an untagged LIST response followed by an untagged STATUS response with the requested information.

If STATUS fails because the mailbox cannot be selected, the STATUS response MUST NOT be returned and the LIST response MUST include the \NoSelect attribute. The server may therefore have to buffer the LIST reply until the lookup succeeds. If the server hits unexpected problems, it MAY drop the STATUS reply, and the LIST command still returns a tagged OK.
sections.eli5: For every box you ask about, the server gives its name and then its counts. If a box cannot be opened, you only get the name, marked as unopenable.

sections.title: Examples
sections.content:
In the first example, A01 LIST "" % RETURN (STATUS (MESSAGES UNSEEN)) returns INBOX with 17 messages and 16 unseen, and foo with 30 messages and 29 unseen. The mailbox bar is not selectable, so it has a LIST response with \NoSelect and no STATUS reply.

In the second, LIST (SUBSCRIBED RECURSIVEMATCH) with the same return option gives STATUS only for INBOX. The LIST reply for foo appears because it has matching children, but foo itself does not match the selection criteria, so it gets no STATUS reply.
sections.eli5: The examples show a client asking for counts and getting a name and numbers per box, with a plain name for a box that cannot be opened.

sections.title: Formal Syntax
sections.content: The syntax uses ABNF and takes terms from RFC 3501 and RFC 5258. It adds one rule: a status-option is the word STATUS, a space, and a parenthesized, space-separated list of status-att items. It follows the option-extension syntax.
sections.eli5: The grammar rule says you write STATUS and then, in brackets, which counts you want.

sections.title: Security and IANA Notes
sections.content:
The extension makes it a bit easier for clients to overload a server by asking for STATUS on many mailboxes, but existing clients already do that with many STATUS commands. While retrieving STATUS for big lists, a server needs to keep serving other IMAP connections and yield execution when necessary.

IANA added the LIST-STATUS capability to the IMAP 4 Capabilities registry and registered the STATUS option, of type RETURN, in the LIST-EXTENDED options registry.
sections.eli5: Asking for lots of counts at once can keep the server busy, so it must still make time for everyone else.
